Featured Case Study

Meal Subscription Management System

Status: In Progress · Portfolio Case Study

A simulated end-to-end business analysis and data analytics engagement for a meal subscription operation whose customer, subscription, order, payment, and delivery activities were being managed across separate Excel files and WhatsApp conversations.

The case study covers business case development, stakeholder analysis, BRD requirements, As-Is / To-Be process mapping, Agile backlog design in Jira, data cleaning, SQL analysis, KPI definition, Excel reporting, and Power BI dashboarding.

Scope transparency: the project uses simulated data, historical reporting, and solution design. Production software development, real-time Power BI connectivity, bank integrations, GPS tracking, and real-company implementation are outside the documented scope.

Project at a glance

Agile / ScrumJiradraw.ioSQLExcelPower BIData Modeling
  • Business problem: duplicated/incomplete data, delayed updates, manual reporting, order & delivery risk.
  • BA outputs: Business Case, BRD, stakeholder register, requirements, rules, acceptance criteria, process maps.
  • Agile outputs: 7 epics, 16 user stories, 14 subtasks, 3 planned sprints, 83 story points.
  • Analytics outputs: cleaned dataset, 11 SQL analyses, Excel analysis, Power BI dashboard.
Business Problem

Fragmented operations

  • Separate Excel files and WhatsApp threads.
  • Duplicate and incomplete customer records.
  • Difficulty tracking subscription status and payments.
  • Delayed updates across customer service, finance, kitchen, and delivery.
  • No centralized management dashboard.
Proposed Direction

Centralized, traceable workflow

  • Single customer/subscription record with validation.
  • Defined lifecycle statuses and business rules.
  • System-supported order generation and delivery updates.
  • Structured data relationships from customer to delivery.
  • Refreshable KPIs and management reporting.

Data Work

Cleaning, validation, modeling, and SQL analysis

Data-quality evidence

1,050 → 1,019 customer rows31 duplicate customer rows were removed from the working customer dataset.
4 invalid subscription date records → 0End-date validation was applied so end dates no longer precede start dates.
11 missing meal names made explicitMissing values were standardized to an explicit “Unknown Meal” category rather than left blank.
Text and category standardizationCity values and order-status capitalization were normalized to consistent categories.
Validation backlog retainedTransaction-reference uniqueness, negative delivery delays, and failed-delivery completeness were also flagged as quality checks rather than silently ignored.

Logical data model

Primary relationship chain: Customer → Subscription → Order → Delivery, with Payments linked to Subscription.

SQL analysis - 11 business questions

01 Executive KPIs
02 Subscription performance by plan
03 Cancellation reasons by plan
04 Order status distribution
05 Top 10 ordered meals
06 Delivery status distribution
07 Delivery performance by time slot
08 Payment status distribution
09 Paid revenue by payment method
10 Geographic performance
11 Monthly revenue + MoM change
-- Example: monthly paid revenue and month-over-month change
WITH MonthlyRevenue AS (...)
SELECT RevenueMonth, PaidRevenueJOD, PreviousMonthRevenue,
  PaidRevenueJOD - PreviousMonthRevenue AS RevenueChangeJOD
FROM RevenueComparison ORDER BY RevenueMonth;

INSIGHT 01

Salt has the largest customer base

145 customer records - the highest among the eight cities in the cleaned dataset.

INSIGHT 02

Volume and value leaders differ

Balanced Living has the most subscriptions (143), while Muscle Gain has the highest contract value (31,440 JOD).

INSIGHT 03

Card leads paid revenue

Card payments contribute 21,757.50 JOD, the highest paid-revenue amount among payment methods.

INSIGHT 04

Morning delivery slot runs slower

10:00 AM-12:00 PM averages 38.16 minutes delay versus 35.41 minutes for 12:00 PM-2:00 PM, suggesting a capacity review opportunity.

Project Impact & Value Designed

What the solution is designed to improve

Efficiency Gain

The To-Be process removes repeated customer searching, duplicate re-entry, manual daily-order preparation, and disconnected status updates by centralizing records and automating key steps.

Designed impact - not production-measured

Data Accuracy

Validation rules, duplicate checks, controlled categories, and documented business rules reduce the risk of inconsistent customer, subscription, order, payment, and delivery information.

Measured example: 31 duplicate customer rows removed

Management Visibility

The dashboard consolidates revenue, subscription, order, and delivery KPIs into a refreshable management view with City and Plan filters.

Historical dashboard - no real-time connection in current scope

No percentage time saving, error-elimination rate, or production ROI is claimed because implementation in a real company is outside the project scope.
